standard.title: Refine movement skills
standard.description: refine and apply fundamental movement skills in new movement situations
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have practised fundamental movement skills and applied them in a variety of movement situations (AC9HP2M01). They can apply skills across locomotor and object control domains in familiar contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students refine and apply fundamental movement skills in new and varied movement situations.

nodes.label: Combining locomotor and object control skills
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform activities that combine locomotor and object control skills to complete a movement task or challenge.
nodes.minimum_width: Combine at least one locomotor skill with one object control skill to complete a set movement task.
nodes.typical_width: Perform a range of activities that combine locomotor and object control skills across different movement tasks and challenges, including games contexts.
wider: Design and perform their own combined-skill movement challenge, explaining the locomotor and object control components involved.
Compare how the combination of locomotor and object control skills differs across two distinct movement contexts (e.g. a field game vs a court game).
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot integrate locomotor and object control skills in combination, they cannot access the refinement and adaptation work in subsequent nodes — all applied movement tasks in this band require combined-skill execution.

response_modes.reason: Students who can execute skills in isolation but not in combination need structured practice that gradually introduces dual demands — locomotor task first, then add the object control component.

success_criteria: Identifies the locomotor and object control components in a given movement task.
Performs a combined-skill movement task, demonstrating coordination between the two skill types.
Completes the movement task or challenge with at least partial success.

nodes.label: Propelling objects towards targets
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore and practise different techniques to propel objects towards a range of targets.
nodes.minimum_width: Practise at least two different techniques for propelling an object towards a stationary target.
nodes.typical_width: Explore and compare multiple propelling techniques across varied objects and target types (distance, accuracy, height), identifying what makes each technique effective.
wider: Investigate how adjusting force, angle or body position changes the outcome when propelling objects towards targets of different sizes and distances.
Apply propelling techniques in a game or challenge context where target type changes across rounds, and reflect on which techniques were most effective.

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a range of propelling techniques across different objects and target configurations — depth in one technique is less useful than breadth across contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Propelling techniques vary richly across object type (ball, beanbag, disc), force demand, and target configuration — wider students who explore this range build substantially more transferable object control capability.
success_criteria: Demonstrates at least two different techniques for propelling an object.
Adjusts their technique when the target changes (e.g. closer vs further, larger vs smaller).
Describes what they changed in their technique and why.

nodes.label: Weight transference in movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform fundamental movement skills that demonstrate weight transference in different physical activities.
nodes.minimum_width: Perform a movement activity that involves transferring body weight (e.g. a roll, step pattern or balance transition), identifying where weight transfer occurs.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate weight transference across a range of physical activities — gymnastics, dance, games — and explain how weight transfer contributes to the movement.
wider: Explore how weight transference principles apply across culturally diverse movement forms such as martial arts, traditional dance, or First Nations Australian movement practices.
Design a short movement sequence that deliberately highlights weight transference at three different points, and coach a peer using appropriate vocabulary.

response_modes.reason: Students often perform weight transference implicitly without conceptual awareness of it. Scaffolding the language and identification of weight transfer — 'where does the weight go, when, and why' — develops the awareness needed to apply it deliberately.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one point in a movement activity where weight is transferred.
Performs a movement that involves deliberate weight transference.
Describes how transferring weight supports the movement outcome.

nodes.label: Coordinated swimming strokes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can coordinate kicking with arm movements to move their body through the water using different types of strokes.
nodes.minimum_width: Coordinate kicking and arm movements to sustain one swimming stroke across at least a short distance.
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate coordination across two or more swimming strokes, sustaining rhythm and timing between kick and arm action across varied distances.
wider: Explore how the coordination demands differ between freestyle and breaststroke — or between any two strokes with different timing patterns — and explain what makes each challenging.
Apply coordinated stroke technique in a minor water-based activity or challenge, adjusting technique in response to feedback.

response_modes.reason: Swimming stroke coordination requires timing precision between two independent movement chains (kick and arms). Students need repeated practice to build automaticity before they can apply skill in varied water contexts.

success_criteria: Coordinates kicking and arm movements in at least one swimming stroke.
Sustains the stroke across a short distance without stopping.
Identifies whether their kick and arm timing felt coordinated and what they would adjust.
nodes.notes: Context-dependent: only applicable where swimming is part of the school program. Where not available, this node may be noted as not assessed.

nodes.label: Movement sequences — jumping, landing and balancing
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can perform and connect movement sequences incorporating different jumping, landing and balancing techniques.
nodes.minimum_width: Perform a movement sequence that connects at least a jump, a landing and a balance, with controlled transitions.
nodes.typical_width: Create and perform a sequence that incorporates multiple jumping, landing and balancing techniques with controlled connections and smooth transitions.
wider: Choreograph and perform a movement sequence for an audience (class or small group), incorporating transitions that are deliberate and match a chosen theme or musical structure.
Compare how jumping, landing and balancing techniques feature in gymnastics, dance and outdoor/adventure activities — identifying similarities and differences in technique demands.
nodes.hinge_reason: Sequencing and connecting movements is the integration demand that spans the whole standard. Students who cannot connect skill components into a sequence will be unable to demonstrate the 'new movement situations' requirement at the progression endpoint, and this limitation cascades into AC9HP6M01 where more complex combined sequences are expected.

response_modes.reason: This node requires students to coordinate previously practised individual skills (jump, land, balance) into a connected sequence. Teacher investment should focus on the transitions — the linking moments — rather than re-teaching individual skills.
Students who achieve the minimum sequence benefit from performing in different movement contexts (gymnastics, dance, outdoor) to build transferability of the sequencing capability.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Sequencing work has rich potential across gymnastic, expressive, and game-based contexts — students who explore the same skills across contexts build substantially more versatile movement capability.
success_criteria: Performs a movement sequence that includes a jump, landing and balance with controlled transitions.
Maintains balance and control at the connection points between elements.
Describes the sequence they performed and at least one aspect they would refine.
